events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph first.** I'd expect it to be the best of the four for the pier, but that is my inference, not a pier report.
- **Expect slow pier fishing everywhere.** My pier ratings are St. Joseph 1-2, South Haven 1, Grand Haven 1, Muskegon 1 (0 slow to 4 excellent).
- **If you fish the pier, use the lowest-effort approach:** spoons and meat rigs, fished as deep as the pier allows, and check the pierhead water before you go.
- **Boat is the better bet this week.** The Aug 3 reports rated boat fishing at St. Joseph good and Muskegon good, but the fish were deep.

## Why

- No pier reports exist for these four ports in the last four weeks; every recent salmon report is from a boat, so the pier ratings above are my estimate.
- I'd expect pier anglers to struggle because the fish were 65-140 feet down in 100-250 feet of water (Muskegon and Grand Haven, Aug 3), well beyond what a pier reaches.
- St. Joseph is my first pick because its Aug 3 boat report was the strongest of the four ("Salmon fishing was good") and said fish moved in late in the week.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (all boat, all Aug 3 unless noted)**
- St. Joseph: "Salmon fishing was good." Meat rigs and spoons, 100+ ft of water, fish moved in toward the end of the week (St. Joseph, 2026-08-03 bulletin, quality 3).
- Muskegon: fish 65-130 ft down in 140-250 ft of water; glow spoons, meat rigs, green or white flies; "The bite was good during low light conditions" (Muskegon, 2022-08-03, quality 3).
- Grand Haven: "Boat anglers found the salmon action to be fair" in 120-220 ft; best bite 65-140 ft down on green flies and meat rigs (Grand Haven, 2022-08-03, quality 2).
- South Haven: "Salmon fishing was on the slow side," best water about 100 ft; a mixed bag of lake trout and Chinook on spoons (South Haven, 2022-08-03, quality 1).
- Earlier, July 14 reports were slow at Grand Haven and Muskegon (quality 0), and St. Joseph had a below-average week July 20 (quality 1). The trend has improved since mid-July.

**Past seasons**
- The similar-temperature search returned only the same recent weeks (about 76 F surface water). It turned up no earlier-season matches, so I have no history to add.

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water near 76 F for the week before Aug 9 at all four ports (buoys 45026, 45168, 45029). The tool was in backtest mode, so this is a summary of the prior week, not live readings.
- Pierhead water temperature and the wind forecast were not returned, so I can't check for upwelling. That is the main thing that would lift pier catches.
- For reference (general guidance, Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension): mature Chinook in early fall hold in water of 55 F or less, and north or east winds can bring cold water and salmon to pierheads. At 76 F, the fish are holding deep, so pier action is unlikely without an upwelling.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are from Aug 3, six days old, and every one is a boat report. The pier ratings are my estimates from boat data.
- The condition data is a backtest summary from the week before Aug 9, not live. Pierhead temperature and wind were unavailable, so I couldn't check for upwelling.
- Check the pierhead temperature and wind before you go. A sharp drop in pierhead water temperature, or a north or east wind, would raise my ratings.

## Sources

- DNR bulletin, Aug 3 (all four ports): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3268d0b
- DNR bulletin, July 20 (St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/323f6bf
- DNR bulletin, July 14 (Grand Haven, Muskegon): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/321350c
